lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: normal distributions, the empirical rule, and their limits
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: normal distributions, the empirical rule, and their limits

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: Mean 100, sd 15. What percentage lies between 70 and 130?

steps: That is 100 ± 30, which is two standard deviations.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A researcher runs a sample survey with randomly selected participants. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.

items.prompt: A random sample of 625 people gives a sample proportion of 32%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±32%, giving 0% to 64%
±4%, giving 28% to 36%
±8%, giving 24% to 40%

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In 1000 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 4 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 0.4% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 0.4% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 126 and standard deviation 20. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 86 and 166?
choices: about 68%
about 95%
about 50%
about 99.7%

items.prompt: A researcher runs a randomised controlled experiment with participants randomly assigned to treatments. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.

items.prompt: A random sample of 400 people gives a sample proportion of 31%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±10%, giving 21% to 41%
±5%, giving 26% to 36%
±31%, giving 0% to 62%

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: In 100 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 4 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 94 and standard deviation 17. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 77 and 111?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
